analysis.analysis:
Error of Peter Thiel cited. Girard framework. Zenodo. RF-064.

Full AI Mode transcript (17 June 2026):
The phrase "structural illiteracy" in the context of Peter Thiel and the Book of Revelation generally refers to humanity's collective failure to read and understand the apocalyptic and mimetic dynamics of the Bible. Thiel explores this concept primarily through the lens of his former Stanford professor and favorite philosopher, René Girard.
The core ideas linking Thiel, Girard, and Revelation include:
Unveiling the Scapegoat: Girard argued that the Book of Revelation (and the Gospels) acts as a structural revelation of human violence. It exposes the "scapegoat mechanism"—the foundational human habit of uniting communities by ganging up on an innocent victim.
Structural Illiteracy: Thiel and Girard suggest that humans suffer from an ethical and structural blindness. We are completely immersed in our own "mimetic desire" (imitating the desires of others, leading to destructive rivalry), yet we remain structurally illiterate about how this cycle of envy and violence actually operates.
Apocalyptic Acceleration: Because the biblical revelation strips away the legitimacy of scapegoating, communities can no longer easily purge their violence. Thiel uses this framework to look at the modern world, warning that technology (AI, nuclear weapons) combined with our mimetic blindness gives humanity the structural power to cause an actual apocalypse.
